actions: Review exact PR head, all 20 logical removals, expected three generated ConfigMap rotations and nine consumers/contracts.

executionProcedure.gate: separately authorized merge and normal Flux convergence
actions: Removal of apps-mop with observed prune=true and default MirrorPrune deletes its unprotected namespace and claims. The two Delete-reclaim CSI PVs trigger native Longhorn data/snapshot/replica disposal. This is intentionally irreversible after independent review; no unobserved retention step is assumed.

Cross-owner MoP receiver RBAC and runtime binding prune independently. Controllers may retry during namespace termination. Verify all surviving Flux owners converge, both retired children are absent and no desired owner can recreate the applications.

Let normal garbage collection remove MoP Pods/ReplicaSets/ControllerRevisions/EndpointSlices, matching Longhorn children and the dedicated RWX share manager. Verify exact volume and snapshot IDs disappear; never force finalizers, delete replica files or modify shared policies.
The NFS PV itself is Flux-pruned, but Retain reclaim and an NFS source leave NAS data intact.

Verify WotLK endpoints, databases, assets and game connectivity, eight Ready runtime agents and remaining security/incident functions. Static local checks are not live acceptance. Do not excuse stale/missing remaining evidence.

OpenBrew is absent from desired state and has no active pods; its namespace and both claims retain prune=disabled. Refresh every namespaced API-object inventory, consumer, CSI/Longhorn attachment and restore/clone reference before deleting.

For each listed claim, review name/UID and fetch fresh resourceVersion; submit DeleteOptions with UID/resourceVersion preconditions to the exact apiPath. Delete one claim at a time, verify normal Delete-reclaim CSI cleanup, then handle the next claim.

After both PVC/PV/Longhorn volume chains are gone, delete only namespace openbrew with its exact reviewed UID and fresh resourceVersion. Verify no recreation. A conflict, changed identity or stuck finalizer stops cleanup; do not separately race-delete PVs.

actions: Refresh Longhorn remote inventory for precisely the four volume handles. Verify every Backup URL, volume/target label, BackupVolume owner UID, completion state and absence of any restore/clone/CSI snapshot-content dependency. Require no in-flight backup/restore; capture an unchanged inventory of unrelated volumes, backups and SystemBackups.

Delete only the reviewed exact dedicated native Backup records via the supported Longhorn workflow, one at a time with fresh UID/resourceVersion preconditions. Verify remote completion after each. Use supported removal of each now-empty dedicated BackupVolume after its history is gone.

The existing general retention helper intentionally retains a last point and must not be repurposed for complete disposal. Do not delete the bucket, shared blocks, BackupTarget, SystemBackups or unrelated history.

Native Backup names beginning system-backup- are volume recovery points, not cluster SystemBackups. Shared archives may describe retired objects; exclude retired identities during future restores, preserving unrelated archive data.

Privately enumerate exact B2 volume prefixes, every object-version/file ID, hide marker, lock, unfinished upload, replication and external copy. These external inventories are unavailable here. Use native cleanup first; any residual direct object-version disposal requires its own exact reviewed ownership list. Do not infer success from disappearance of a CR.
